$comment: Single source of truth for the current cut (Draft 5, voiced: every shot and VO window is fitted to the measured TTS lines in $VIDEO_OUT/vo). Times are video timecodes (m:ss.s) from VIDEO_SCRIPT.md. Source points for stage takes are 'P+x' = seconds after the Play click in that take (takes/<id>.markers.json); for the MCP clip, seconds into takes/mcp-demo.mp4. Anchors {take, event, offset} resolve to the video time at which that stage event is on screen. {T} / {T_words} / {BLOCK_T} / {TESTS} are filled from the recorded stopwatch and the real test run. build.mjs validates every VO line against its window at its target wpm and prints the fit.

vo.text: Mrs. Lan doesn't read English, and her power's been out two days. She just left a voice note. Watch the clock.
She heard it read back in Vietnamese and said yes. The group's own rules, not the AI, set the amount: a hundred and fifty dollars. Two organizers sign.

vo.note: Starts 0.6 s before the cut to her phone: "Paid," over the three paid phones, the cut in the pause after it.

text.sandbox: Paid, into her Venmo, with a message in Vietnamese. {T_words} seconds to PayPal's SUCCESS webhook. The approvals came on cue; real neighbors take longer.
text.fake: Paid, into her Venmo, with a message in Vietnamese. {T_words} seconds to the SUCCESS webhook, on our PayPal stand-in. The approvals came on cue; real neighbors take longer.

vo.text: This is Neighborline: a hotline, not a dashboard. After the Eaton fire, one LA mutual-aid network took three hundred requests overnight, in Instagram comments. Most still run on a volunteer's personal Venmo.
Rosa asks for groceries, in Spanish. Same rules, two approvals.

vo.note: Starts 1.5 s before UNCLAIMED lands, so the word "unclaimed" is spoken just after it is on screen.
vo.text: Her email has no PayPal account yet: unclaimed. She gets claim help in Spanish.

vo.note: "Success." is spoken ~0.7 s after SUCCEEDED is on screen.
vo.text: She claims it. Success. Most payout systems stop at unclaimed; this one follows through.
Someone posing as the organizers, with a Venmo handle one letter off? Approve is disabled on every phone. No money moves.

vo.note: Runs over /trust and into the rail push (Shot 10).
vo.text: Under the hood: the agents that talk to neighbors have no PayPal tools. One separate approval service holds the Payouts credentials, and it pays only on a record signed with the passkeys of two different organizers.
AI output is schema-checked, repaired once, or the neighbor is asked again.

vo.note: Card 2 under "can't pay twice", card 3 under "signature-verified", card 4 under "reconciled … real run".
vo.text: The batch ID is derived from the signed approval, so a double tap can't pay twice. Webhooks are signature-verified, and every payout is reconciled against PayPal Transaction Search. The test count is from a real run.
For agent builders: the same guard ships as an MCP server. An AI agent asking to pay is refused without two humans' signatures. With them, it pays.
Donors give with PayPal or Venmo. The public report never names a neighbor, and every number comes from the ledger.
Neighborline is open source. Try the hotline yourself; the link is below. Because the morning after a storm, help should sound like your own language.
